transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-06
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jesse Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Alex Lopez (CTO - Meridian Works), Priya Nair (Head of ML), Devon Chen (Senior Backend)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough):
- Meridian Works evaluating Redwood for PLG/self-serve API to enable an in-app assistant and embeddings for search.
- Key concerns: time-to-first-token, free credits for evaluation, data residency/SOC2, and potential future Dedicated/Private deployment for PII workloads.
- Next steps: send quickstart, provision sandbox credits, schedule infra deep dive for dedicated/private requirements.

Topics: quickstart flow, free credits, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, security/compliance, benchmarking and pilot scope, timeline and success criteria.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jesse: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I'm Jesse from Redwood, i'm the a e on this account. uh before we jump in can we do quick intros?
[00:07] Alex: yeah alex here, cto, we're evaluating a few vendors for in-app assistant.
[00:11] Priya: priya, head of ml, i'll lead the eval and testing.
[00:15] Devon: devon, backend, i'll own integration and infra questions.
[00:19] Samira: hi all, samira from the se team at redwood, i'll cover quickstart and demo bits.

[00:30] Jesse: cool, agenda — quick overview of redwood quickstart, how free credits and sandbox work, then dig into hosted vs dedicated vs private, then wrap with next steps. sound good?
[00:38] Alex: sounds good.

[01:05] Samira: quickstart is super short — most teams get a token in less than an hour. sign up, create an api key in console, run our curl quickstart or the sdk sample, you can hit text generation, chat, embeddings. we also have preseeded prompt templates for r e s p o n d e r or whatever. (laughter)
[01:28] Priya: when you say under an hour, is that from sign-up to first token for new orgs? like do you require manual approval?
[01:35] Samira: good q — for PLG quickstart it's fully self-serve. account creation is instant; we provision a sandbox org with free credits automatically for new sign-ups. sometimes for higher-rate limits we do a low-friction verification but usually first token is minutes.
[01:48] Devon: ok nice. any quotas on the free credits? we want to run a small bench sim and 10k embeddings.
[01:55] Jesse: typical sandbox credits are enough for tens of thousands of tokens and a few thousand embeddings; if you need a larger trial we can up it — samira can do that.

[02:20] Priya: what's the model catalog look like on hosted? can we pick open models or do you provide your own stack?
[02:26] Samira: hosted catalog has a mix — curated open models like mistral variants, llama-family forks, and our verified performance profiles. you can call specific models via the api. for certain enterprise tiers we also offer vetted model bundles.
[02:39] Alex: are you running the models yourselves or using other infra providers?
[02:43] Samira: we run the runtime — we manage serving in our hosted environment. for dedicated and private we offer dedicated g p u pools or customer-managed vpc/on-prem.

[03:05] Devon: for our use-case some user messages contain p i i, so data residency and encryption at rest are a must. how does hosted handle that?
[03:13] Jesse: hosted encrypts in transit and at rest, default retention policies can be configured, and we have enterprise add-ons like private networking and KMS integration. but for strict PII or regulated data we typically recommend Dedicated or Private so customer data never leaves their environment.
[03:29] Priya: is SOC2 available?
[03:31] Jesse: yes we have SOC2 and are working on ISO in some regions — i'll send the SOC2 report.

[03:50] Alex: latency wise, do you have numbers for hosted vs dedicated? we do sub-200ms SLO for short prompts.
[03:58] Samira: hosted p50 for short gen on common models is ~80-120ms p50 depending on model. Dedicated gives more predictable tail latencies because you reserve pools. if you need sub-200ms hard SLOs, dedicated or colocated private infra is the safer bet.

[04:22] Priya: what's the cost delta between hosted and dedicated? we are price sensitive and plan for scale.
[04:28] Jesse: hosted is pay-as-you-go; unit economics are competitive for early scale. Dedicated is commit-based — you get better per-token costs plus predictable throughput. we can run a sizing exercise once we have your traffic profile.

[04:45] Devon: how easy is it to switch from hosted to dedicated when we scale? any migration friction?
[04:51] Samira: we built for portability — same api, same model ids (with versioning). migration is mostly config and routing; some customers do a canary with routing rules. we provide exportable KV caches and compatibility helpers.

[05:20] Alex: ok pilot scope — we want to run embeddings for search across 2M docs and a chat assistant for internal helpdesk. timeline is 6-8 weeks to pilot.
[05:32] Jesse: that aligns well. quickstart -> sandbox for feature dev + small benchmark -> pilot with dedicated sizing if needed. success criteria?
[05:40] Priya: three things: accuracy of embeddings/retrieval, p95 latency under 300ms for search, and cost per 1k queries under a threshold. i'll share exact numbers.

[06:10] Samira: for embeddings we recommend batch embedding endpoints and prefix caching; we'll send best practices. embeddings batching reduces per-item cost.

[06:27] Devon: on the sdk side, do you have example microservices for streaming responses and handling the kv cache?
[06:33] Samira: yes — node/python/ go samples, plus a small reference app that shows streaming, tool-calls, and cache hints. link in the quickstart doc.

[07:00] Alex: security — can you support SSO, SAML, RBAC at the org level?
[07:06] Jesse: yes sso/saml, oauth, role-based access, audit logs on enterprise plans. we also have per-route api keys and token-level cost/call attribution.

[07:28] Priya: curious about model regression monitoring — we need guardrails when we switch model versions.
[07:33] Samira: we have Redwood Optimize tooling: quality monitoring against eval sets, regression alerts, and can integrate with your eval pipelines. we'll send the eval template.

[07:55] Alex: ok comps — we're also talking to openai and anthropic, mainly on latency and model quality. any pitfalls we should know about moving from those to redwood?
[08:04] Jesse: main differences: redwood focuses on production serving and cost controls. if you rely on specific proprietary models from openai, you'll see different quality tradeoffs. we prioritize predictable latency, batching, and custom routing to optimize cost while keeping quality.

[08:30] Devon: does your hosted environment let us pin model versions? we want reproducible outputs.
[08:35] Samira: yes model pinning and versioned endpoints are supported — you can pin at route level and roll out canaries.

[09:00] Priya: for evaluation, can we get raw token-level logs and traces for debugging?
[09:06] Jesse: audit logs and traces are available on enterprise; for sandbox you'll get request/response logs but token-level retention is configurable. we'll share default retention settings.

[09:30] Alex: about private deployments — can you run in our vpc? we're also exploring air-gapped on-prem for some customers.
[09:38] Samira: yes we have private deployment options: customer-managed vpc with private control plane, and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. that typically involves an enterprise agreement and a few weeks for deployment.

[10:05] Devon: networking — how do you handle egress to third-party model registries or updates?
[10:11] Samira: in private mode we can disable any external egress; in dedicated we control egress rules and images are curated by us. for hosted we manage model hosting so no external pull is needed.

[10:40] Alex: one practical question — what's the path for us to get started this week? we want to spin up a sandbox and test embedding accuracy.
[10:48] Jesse: i'll send an invite with the quickstart link and samira will provision sandbox credits. you can get an api key and run sample embeddings in under an hour.

[11:12] Samira: i'll also include a small benchmark script we use internally — it's idempotent and simulates your qps. send us a small sample of your payloads and we'll tune.

[11:35] Priya: what's the expected cost for a month-long pilot if we're embedding 2M docs? rough estimate is fine.
[11:42] Jesse: rough hosted cost might be higher; for that volume we usually recommend a dedicated sizing call. we'll do a quick cost model with your docs size.

[12:05] Devon: are there throttles or rate limits on the sandbox keys that would block realistic testing?
[12:11] Samira: sandbox keys have conservative rate limits by default but we can bump them for trials. for realistic bench we lift limits temporarily.

[12:35] Alex: ok let's talk timeline: we want to start dev this week, run bench next week, and converge on pilot by end of month.
[12:43] Jesse: sounds good. i'll draft a timeline in the follow-up email.

[13:05] Priya: one last question — quantization and model size. do you offer quantized model variants for cost saving?
[13:11] Samira: yes we serve quantized variants and recommend them for cost-sensitive workloads; we can show perf/cost tradeoffs.

[13:32] Jesse: great — let's recap next steps quickly.
[13:35] Alex: sure.

[13:36] Jesse: action items: 1) Jesse sends pricing and quickstart link; 2) Samira provisions sandbox and lift limits for their bench; 3) Samira sends benchmark script and model recommendations; 4) Alex shares traffic profile and SLOs.
[13:50] Devon: noted.

[14:05] Priya: thanks all, this was helpful.
[14:08] Samira: thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and SOC2.
[14:12] Jesse: thanks everyone, talk soon.

[14:30] call ends

Notes about transcription quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms (e.g., kv cache transcribed as k v cash), some names may be misspelled.

Referenced artifacts / links mentioned: Quickstart guide (link sent in follow-up), Sandbox org provisioning note, Benchmark script (attached in follow-up), SOC2 report (to be shared).
